findings.body: The doc comment lists exactly four valid values: `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high`. Storing them as a `String` means any arbitrary string compiles and will be passed to the model, which may reject it or silently ignore it. The rest of the config struct uses typed fields (`u32`, `f64`, `Vec<String>`); a `String` here stands out as untyped and will produce silent failures at runtime. Fix: define an enum or use a constants set, and validate on deserialization.
findings.title: Use an enum or constant set for reasoning_effort instead of String

findings.body: The doc comment for `reasoning_effort` promises four values (`off`, `low`, `medium`, `high`) but the field itself is an unvalidated `String`. A value like `"Off"` (capitalised), `"auto"`, or a typo will be silently accepted and passed to the model, likely producing a runtime error that the caller cannot diagnose from the config. This is a concrete, reachable input: any user-supplied config file or CLI argument that sets `reasoning_effort` to a string not in the documented set will compile and run, then fail. The doc comment also says `off` "is the setting that rescues a deployment whose model reasons past `max_tokens`", which implies this is a load-bearing feature that the user must be able to rely on — silent acceptance of an invalid value defeats that reliability.
findings.title: Validate reasoning_effort against the documented values

value.summary: Adds a `reasoning_effort` field as a plain `String` without validation, which is both a regression against the existing typed pattern and an omission of the documented enum values. The diff itself shows the two issues: a raw string where a typed enum or constant set is expected, and no validation that the value is one of the four documented choices.
